insight: When materializing decomposed epics in beads on a repo whose directory contains a dot (e.g. ryanhenderson.dev), bd init writes .beads/metadata.json with dolt_database equal to the directory name; embedded Dolt rejects dots and bd commands fail with 'invalid database name'. Fix: edit .beads/metadata.json dolt_database to the underscore-form (ryanhenderson_dev) which matches the existing .beads/embeddeddolt subdirectory bd already created.

For solo-dev personal sites, the architect's decomposition should fold cross-cutting concerns (single-source helpers, build-time smoke tests, scoped tokens, CSP hashes, lazy-load assertions, frozen lockfile) into per-epic acceptance criteria rather than spawning separate cross-cutting epics. Separate 'testing' / 'devops' / 'security' epics fragment ownership and create coordination cost out of proportion to a single-author project. The architect skill's 'Cross-cutting concerns folded into per-epic ACs' table is the right pattern; aim for ~15-20 such concerns mapped to specific epic ACs.

When the advisor fleet flags YAGNI items (e.g. Atom-alongside-RSS, scripted DNS, Satori OG) but the user has explicitly chosen them, do NOT silently drop them in decomposition. Honor the user's choice, embed the advisor's mitigations as non-negotiable per-epic ACs (e.g. scoped CF token, static fallback PNG, RSS draft-leak smoke test), and surface the kept-vs-dropped negotiation explicitly at Gate 2 so the trade-off is auditable.

When testing Astro 5 content collection schemas (zod), extract the schema definitions into a pure module (e.g. src/content/schemas.ts) and have src/content/config.ts import them and wire them into defineCollection. Then test the schemas directly with vitest -- they no longer require booting the astro:content / astro/loaders virtual modules. The schema's .strict() rejection, default values, and required-field enforcement become unit-testable in isolation. Without this split, vitest can't import config.ts because astro:content only resolves during astro dev/build.

Grep-style enforcement scripts (e.g. forbidding direct getCollection() calls outside a single helper module) MUST scan whole-file with multi-line regex (text.matchAll on the raw string) and compute line numbers from match index, NOT split on 
 and run a per-line regex. A per-line scan misses multi-line calls like getCollection(
  "blog"
) and aliased imports like { getCollection as gc } from "astro:content". Pin the enforcement with integration tests that exercise: (a) the happy path, (b) a single-line offender, (c) a multi-line call, (d) an aliased import, and (e) an unrelated function with the same name (false-positive guard). Without the integration tests, a regression in the regex silently disables the gate.

Astro 5's content layer glob loader derives entry id from the relative path within base, NOT from the basename. So src/content/blog/foo.mdx and src/content/blog/sub/foo.mdx coexist with distinct ids ('foo' and 'sub/foo') and Astro itself does NOT detect the slug collision. If the spec requires within-collection slug uniqueness (slug = filename minus .mdx), you need a separate pre-build gate (e.g. scripts/check-content-slugs.mjs) that walks each collection directory and flags duplicate basenames across paths. This is independent of Astro's own validation and is the only way to catch the 'two files render at the same URL' failure mode before the build.

For Astro projects, 'pnpm lint' should run 'astro check' (not bare tsc). astro check feeds .astro templates and the generated .astro/types.d.ts (CollectionEntry types) through TypeScript so type errors in component frontmatter and content collection consumers surface together. Bare tsc misses .astro files entirely. When set up: install @astrojs/check, add 'lint': 'astro check' to package.json, and gate CI on it.

Design tokens that need to drive both CSS variables AND build-time renderers (Satori for OG images, Shiki for syntax highlighting) must live in a single TypeScript module — Satori cannot resolve CSS custom properties, so concrete hex/numeric values are mandatory. Generate tokens.css from tokens.ts via a small Node script wired into pnpm build (Node 22.6+ runs .ts via type-stripping; .mjs scripts can dynamic-import .ts). Enforce zero drift with a vitest test that compares tokensToCss() output to the committed CSS file. Reserve consumer-side variable names (e.g. --shiki-fg) inside the token module so downstream epics cannot drift them.

Astro CSS scoping injects 'data-astro-cid-*' attributes between authored attributes; tests asserting attribute order with simple regex break. Use [^>]* between attrs or parse the tag, not literal-order regex.
On routes with noindex (e.g. 404), do NOT emit <link rel=canonical>. A canonical on a noindex page tells crawlers to treat that URL as the canonical destination — semantically backwards.

Skip-link CLS trap: switching from position:absolute(off-screen) to position:static on :focus reflows the page when keyboard users tab in. Use translateY(-200%) → translateY(0) so the link stays absolutely positioned in both states. Required to keep CLS=0.

When multiple Vitest files all assert against `dist/` produced by `pnpm build`, putting `execSync('pnpm build')` in each file's `beforeAll` causes parallel build invocations to race on the same output paths and produce intermittent failures. Solution: consolidate the build into Vitest's `globalSetup` (run once before any suite) and have each test file just verify the artifacts it expects already exist. See vitest.config.ts `globalSetup: ['./tests/setup/build.ts']` pattern in this repo.

Astro emits HTML attributes in source-declaration order, not a guaranteed order. Tests that chain multiple attributes in a single regex (e.g. /class="x"[^>]*href="y"[^>]*target=/) are brittle: they break when authors reorder the source attributes or after Astro upgrades. Capture the tag with /<a\b[^>]*>/g, filter by a stable selector (a class or data-* hook), then assert each attribute with a separate .toMatch on the captured tag.

Astro getStaticPaths runs in an isolated module context — module-scope helpers (functions/consts) declared in the same .astro file are NOT in scope. Inline the logic or export+import from another module. Symptom: 'X is not defined' at build time despite local declaration.

Hand-rolled XML feeds (e.g. Atom) MUST escape ALL attribute values, not just element text. URL strings interpolated into href= or id= produce invalid XML if the URL contains & < > or quotes. Use escapeXml() on every attribute value, even ones that 'look safe'.

Astro check:content-source-style regexes that grep for forbidden patterns (e.g. getCollection("blog")) can match comments and JSDoc text. Rephrase comments to avoid the literal pattern (use 'the raw collection loader' instead of the literal call). Don't weaken the regex.

Satori 0.26 treats children: [] as multi-child and demands explicit display: flex/contents/none on the parent — even though the array is empty. Fix: when building a Satori element tree with a helper, omit the children key entirely for leaf nodes (length 0) instead of passing an empty array. Otherwise hairline divider divs (width/height/backgroundColor only, no children) trigger 'Expected <div> to have explicit display'.

For SEO migration cutover commits (Jekyll → Astro): the retirement commit must atomically include BOTH the deletion of legacy source files AND the public/_redirects file. Splitting them creates a window where audited legacy URLs return 404 (STPA B3 timing issue). Pin this with a test that parses both docs/migration/legacy-urls.txt and public/_redirects and asserts every audited REDIRECT row has a matching rule, and every rule traces back to an audit row — drift in either direction breaks SEO link equity.
